narrative: Sixteen tickets over 13 months show a pattern of quick individual fixes but no lasting stability: the report-builder freeze-on-save recurs at least four times, with the customer noting 'yesterday's fix didn't hold', and problems cluster in multi-day bursts across different modules. The tone drifts from irritated to resigned ('feels like whack-a-mole at the moment') and never turns positive. The most recent tickets (duplicate alerts, an alert configuration that reset itself) close the history still open, with no confirmation the fix actually held.

Four routine, well-spaced tickets over a year — ownership transfer, an API field gap, an alert threshold quirk, a connector schedule change — all reported calmly and closed without complaint or recurrence. No anger, no chasing. A normal, engaged account with no churn signal in the text.

Eight tickets over nine months, evenly spaced and professional throughout — the customer asks for root-cause fixes rather than workarounds ('would like to understand root cause rather than a workaround') but never expresses anger. Two issues (dashboard load time, a report-builder export button affecting a second user) are mentioned twice each but never chased a third time, suggesting they were actually resolved. Resolution times drift upward slightly but haven't dented the relationship.

Only three tickets in a year, but the export-missing-a-tab fault recurs on a different report five months later ('we're seeing the same missing-tab issue Matti flagged back in the autumn'), meaning the original fix didn't generalise. Tone stays even and helpful throughout with no anger, but this is the low-volume, unresolved-underneath pattern worth flagging rather than reading as quiet health.

A genuine escalation arc: intermittent API failures dragged from December into January with rising frustration ('not another "we're looking into it" reply'), culminating in a July request for a call with the team lead after a seat-provisioning issue piled on top of the earlier API problems. The October ticket confirms the call worked — 'things have genuinely been more stable' and 'appreciate the quick response as usual these days' — closing on a clearly positive, resolved note.

A rough first quarter of 2025 (a seat downgrade ignored for weeks, three separate report-builder crashes, a formal demand for senior review) gives way, after a summer intervention, to a run of calm, appreciative tickets through September and October: 'the account has felt noticeably more stable since the changes over the summer' and 'report builder has been rock solid since the summer.' A recovered account — the escalation worked and the customer says so explicitly.

Five tickets over four months, mostly feature requests and how-to questions delivered in a friendly, engaged tone ('Loving the new export options'). One dashboard-sharing-link ticket was logged as unresolved but never chased again, suggesting a minor, low-stakes annoyance rather than a live problem. No risk signal here.

A meticulous, low-drama account that shows a chronic fault never fully closed: alert recipients dropping off a list recurs in May, July ('still happening... would like this properly fixed rather than re-adding people each time') and December ('it's been open on and off since May'), each time marked resolved before recurring again. The report-builder duplicate-template bug follows the same shape. Calm tone shouldn't be mistaken for health here — this is accumulation without real resolution.
A single routine ticket about a secondary alert recipient, resolved in three days with no follow-up. Nothing to act on.

A high-volume account (14 tickets over 18 months) with issues arriving in tight clusters and two faults that genuinely recur — dashboard going blank ('same blank dashboard issue as August, back again') and exports corrupting on download, both reappearing months after being marked resolved. The customer stays transactional rather than despairing, even crediting the team's speed ('your team fixes these fast, credit where due'), but the underlying instability is never actually root-caused across repeated reappearances.

Pekka's tickets grow steadily more pointed across seven months: a security-relevant dashboard-permissions bug takes nine days ('this is not a minor inconvenience... please escalate'), the February export-tabs fault recurs into an April ticket still marked unresolved during Q1 close ('I've lost count of how many tickets we've raised... I'll need to escalate to account management'), and the team is quietly working around a calculated-field bug in spreadsheets ('which rather defeats the purpose'). No positive turn appears before the data ends.

Eight low-stakes tickets over the year — a missing chart type, slow report-builder loading reported twice but mildly, file-naming and layout requests. Tone is even and undramatic throughout with no chasing or escalation. Minor friction, no real risk signal.

Four unrelated, minor tickets spread across 11 months — documentation, an alert-threshold caching quirk, a pagination question, a missing export button — each closed without complaint or recurrence. A quiet, healthy account.

narrative: This is the quiet-risk profile: the /reports pagination bug is reported in December, resurfaces in March ('either it's regressed or the fix was partial'), and returns a third time in August, by which point the customer has built their own client-side dedup logic rather than wait on a fix. The August and September tickets both name a competitor directly, moving from 'trialling Dashlume's API for internal use cases' to 'weighing Dashlume more seriously for next year', while a second recurring fault (missing export rows) gets the same quiet-workaround treatment ('No need to treat this as urgent'). Low volume and calm prose are masking a customer who has stopped expecting fixes and is actively evaluating an alternative ahead of renewal.

Three tickets in a two-month window in 2024 and nothing since — a bulk-export timeout left marked unresolved with no follow-up, plus two routine connector/SSO setup questions. No anger, no chasing, but also no confirmation the export issue was ever fixed, and the account has gone quiet. Worth a routine check-in rather than an alarm.

Fifteen tickets across 14 months with several faults marked resolved and then explicitly returning — the admin-panel error ('same admin panel error from July is back'), the connector sync stall, and the report-builder autosave crash ('the same autosave issue from last summer that never really got addressed') — alongside a two-week silent alerts outage discovered by accident in September. The customer's patience visibly wears down ('I need a straight answer on what's actually unstable') with no turnaround shown before the data ends.

An escalation-heavy 2024–early 2025 (a connector sync delay recurs and worsens across three tickets, culminating in 'I need a proper account review, not more individual tickets') gives way to a markedly calmer run from July onward — 'much quieter few months... appreciate the change since the spring' — though the same connector issue briefly resurfaces that same week and lingers at low grade through July, left unresolved ('still lags... not urgent, but flagging so it's on record'). Recent tickets (API key rotation, rate-limit questions, a template logo update) are routine and unconcerned, suggesting the escalation genuinely worked even if one small root cause was never fully closed.

A genuinely rocky year — API failures recurring three times with a 30-day resolution ('not acceptable for a Professional plan'), a formal call request citing three broken modules, and by July an explicit statement that renewal is in question ('we need to understand what is actually wrong before we can commit to renewing at this level'). August marks a real turn: the API fix holds ('this time the fix came back in three days rather than weeks'), and September–October tickets are calm and appreciative. The turnaround is recent — about two months of good behaviour by year end — and follows an explicit renewal threat, so some caution is still warranted despite the positive trend.

Three tickets, all positive — a report-template question with an unprompted compliment ('the platform has been great to work with so far'), a bulk-seat-management feature request tied to team growth, and a new connector setup ahead of a planning cycle. A healthy, expanding account with no friction in the text.

Only three tickets, but the PDF export layout bug from March is still being worked around in May rather than fixed: 'we've settled into a routine now where the on-screen dashboard gets exported to Excel and reformatted there... No need to prioritise on our end.' That explicit de-prioritising of a real, recurring fault, from a small and otherwise calm account, is exactly the quiet-disengagement pattern worth flagging rather than reading as low-touch health.
